llm.summary: This skill matches its Telegram contract workflow purpose, but it handles government ID and banking data with unsafe storage, group disclosure, and hardcoded personal data in source code.

dimensions.detail: Using Telegram, Node, Python, Swift OCR, and local files is purpose-aligned, but the workflow writes eID images, OCR JSON, parsed identity fields, mapped contract data, and generated documents in plaintext with default permissions and little cleanup.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation guidance uses ClawHub commands and environment files, but recommends unpinned global npm installation for the CLI and does not give strong secret-handling guidance for the Telegram bot token.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The bot scopes access by configured Telegram group only, returns extracted eID fields and optional raw OCR text back to that group, and does not define sender allowlists, private return channels, consent, retention, or debug restrictions for sensitive ID data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The long-running polling bot stores persistent session state under the workspace and leaves sensitive artifacts on disk; this is high-impact for a government-ID workflow without retention controls or restrictive file modes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Telegram contract generation and Vietnamese eID OCR capabilities are coherent with the stated purpose, but the packaged generator embeds a full personal identity/contact/banking record as template-matching text, which is not necessary to install or publish.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Do not deploy this in production until the source and templates are sanitized, Telegram access is restricted to authorized users, sensitive results are returned privately, debug OCR is disabled or admin-only, and all eID/OCR/contract artifacts have documented permissions, cleanup, and retention controls. Treat the hardcoded personal and banking data in the package as exposed.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The Telegram API calls and environment token use are expected for a Telegram bot; I found no non-Telegram webhook or unrelated external destination in the inspected script.
[MP3] expected: The reported state deletion is local bot session cleanup, not agent memory poisoning or persistent instruction modification.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The scanner's privacy concerns are supported: eID screenshots and extracted identity data are processed with no adequate user-facing safeguards, retention limits, masking, or access-control guidance.
[SQP-3] expected: The Vietnamese language and locale choices are consistent with the skill description, which explicitly targets Vietnamese operations and Vietnamese electronic IDs.
[SDI-2] expected: Calling local Python and Swift helper scripts is consistent with the documented architecture and runtime requirements, though the storage behavior around those helpers remains a concern.
[E1] expected: External transmission to api.telegram.org is expected for the declared Telegram bot workflow, not evidence by itself of credential or data exfiltration.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The management-group help text advertises Plan A reminder/report behavior that this package does not implement; this is an implementation mismatch rather than malware evidence.
[T09] unexpected: The SARIF plaintext-retention and hardcoded-personal-data findings are supported by the artifacts and are disproportionate for a published skill handling identity and banking data.
[T05] unexpected: The SARIF authorization concern is supported: any member of the configured contract group can use the sensitive eID workflow, and results are posted to the group rather than restricted to an authorized individual.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned global npm CLI install is not evidence that this skill is malicious, but it is weaker than a pinned or verified installation procedure.
